identity.headquarters: New York, United States (with major engineering presence in Paris, France)

value_chain.value_chain_position: Specialized foundation model creator focused on AI-powered software engineering. Depends on NVIDIA GPUs (GB300 NVL72 systems) and CoreWeave/AWS cloud infrastructure for training and inference. Building vertical integration into compute infrastructure through Project Horizon (2GW data center in West Texas with CoreWeave). Serves enterprise customers with 5,000+ developer teams (major banks, defense contractors) through custom-deployed, fine-tuned coding models. Does not serve general-purpose AI use cases -- purely focused on the software development vertical. Positions between model creation and enterprise application layers by customizing foundation models per-customer on their proprietary codebases.

key_products: Malibu (flagship reasoning model): Deep reasoning model for developer chat and complex software engineering tasks. Built from scratch (not fine-tuned from an existing open model). Designed for enterprise deployment within customer security boundaries. Fine-tuned on each customer's proprietary codebase and development history to understand organization-specific patterns, libraries, and coding standards.

Point (code completion model): AI-powered code completion engine integrated into developer workflows. Provides real-time suggestions as developers write code. Like Malibu, customized per-customer by ingesting the customer's existing codebase and development history. Deployed within client infrastructure for security -- code never leaves the customer's environment.

Poolside Platform (enterprise AI coding platform): End-to-end platform for deploying AI coding assistance across large engineering organizations. Includes dedicated training environments spun up within client infrastructure, codebase ingestion and fine-tuning pipelines, and integration across multiple developer surfaces (IDE, chat, CI/CD). Targeting enterprises with 5,000+ developers.

business.revenue_or_valuation: Valued at $3B following $500M Series B (Oct 2024). Reportedly raising $2B at $12B valuation as of Oct 2025, with $1B+ already committed including $500M-$1B from NVIDIA. Revenue reached $50M in 2025, up from $30M in 2024. 256 employees as of 2025.
business.annual_recurring_revenue_arr: [uncertain] Revenue reported at $50M in 2025 (up from $30M in 2024). Given enterprise contract model with multi-year deals, most revenue is likely recurring, but exact ARR figure not publicly confirmed.
business.funding_total_and_last_round: Total raised: ~$626M through Series B (as of Oct 2024). Seed: $26M (May 2023). Additional early round: ~$100M (mid-2023). Series B: $500M (Oct 2024) at $3B valuation, led by Bain Capital Ventures with participation from eBay Ventures, NVIDIA, LG Technology Ventures, Felicis Ventures, Redpoint Ventures, Citi Ventures, Capital One Ventures, HSBC Ventures, DST Global, StepStone Group, Schroders Capital, Premji Invest, Dorsal Capital, Bpifrance. New round: reportedly raising $2B at $12B valuation (Oct 2025), with NVIDIA investing $500M-$1B.
business.business_model: Enterprise software licensing with custom deployment. B2B model targeting organizations with 5,000+ developers. For each customer, Poolside spins up dedicated training environments within client infrastructure, ingests proprietary codebases, and fine-tunes models specifically for that organization. Revenue from enterprise contracts (likely annual or multi-year subscriptions). Not a generic API provider -- each deployment is customized. Additional distribution through AWS Bedrock for managed deployment. Business model avoids the commoditization risk of generic API pricing by delivering organization-specific AI coding assistants that improve with each customer's data.
business.burn_rate_and_runway: [uncertain] Not publicly disclosed. With $626M raised through Series B, $50M revenue in 2025, and significant infrastructure investment (Project Horizon, 40,000+ NVIDIA GPUs), burn rate is likely substantial. If the $2B raise at $12B valuation closes (Oct 2025 reports), runway extends significantly. Heavy compute investment suggests burn rate well above revenue.

openness.open_vs_closed_spectrum: Closed. Both Malibu and Point models are proprietary and deployed exclusively within customer security boundaries. No open-weight releases, no public API. Product is not available to individual developers or small teams -- enterprise-only. This closed approach is core to the value proposition: models are fine-tuned on each customer's proprietary code, making openness fundamentally incompatible with the business model.

startup_relevance.relevance_for_startups: Poolside represents a significant bet on AI-native software engineering for large enterprises, with several implications for entrepreneurs: (1) Signal of where enterprise AI spend is heading -- major banks (Citi, Capital One, HSBC all investors) and defense contractors are Poolside's target customers, validating that large organizations will pay premium prices for AI coding tools customized to their proprietary codebases rather than using generic solutions like GitHub Copilot. (2) Not accessible to startups as a tool -- Poolside's minimum viable customer has 5,000+ developers, making it irrelevant as a tool for early-stage companies. However, understanding Poolside's approach matters for startups building developer tools or competing in the AI coding space. (3) Competitive threat to GitHub Copilot and generic AI coding assistants -- Poolside's custom fine-tuning approach suggests that one-size-fits-all coding assistants may not satisfy enterprise requirements, creating opportunities for startups that can offer specialized, fine-tuned coding AI for specific verticals or tech stacks at lower scale than Poolside's target market. (4) The Project Horizon infrastructure play (2GW data center, 40,000+ NVIDIA GPUs) shows the capital intensity required to compete at the frontier of AI model training -- a cautionary signal for startups considering building their own foundation models. (5) French/European presence (Paris engineering team, Bpifrance investment) makes Poolside part of the European AI ecosystem despite US headquarters, relevant for French tech policy discussions. (6) Investor roster (NVIDIA, Bain Capital, DST Global, multiple bank venture arms) signals strong institutional conviction in the AI-for-code vertical.
startup_relevance.accessibility: Very low accessibility for startups. Product is enterprise-only, targeting organizations with 5,000+ developers. No public API, no self-serve tier, no individual developer access. Custom deployment requires enterprise sales process and likely six-figure+ annual contracts. Available through AWS Bedrock for managed deployment, but still enterprise-focused. Startups cannot build on Poolside's models or platform. Relevant only as a competitive reference point or market signal, not as a tool to use.
startup_relevance.primary_model_dependency: None. Poolside builds its own foundation models from scratch for software engineering.

AWS (Bedrock integration for managed enterprise deployment; strategic partnership announced Dec 2024 for secure AI coding on Amazon Bedrock and EC2). NVIDIA (major investor with $500M-$1B commitment in 2025 round; GPU supplier; deep technical relationship). Bpifrance (French public investment bank, investor supporting European AI presence). SentinelOne / S Ventures (investor, potential cybersecurity integration for secure code generation). Bain Capital Ventures (lead Series B investor). Multiple bank venture arms (Citi, Capital One, HSBC -- both investors and potential customers).
ecosystem.competitive_moat: Custom per-customer model fine-tuning creates deep switching costs -- once Poolside ingests an organization's entire codebase and development history, the resulting model understands organization-specific patterns, internal libraries, and coding standards that competitors cannot replicate without similar onboarding. Security-first architecture (code never leaves customer boundaries) satisfies regulated industries (banking, defense) that cannot use cloud-based coding assistants. Vertical focus on software engineering allows deeper specialization than general-purpose AI labs dabbling in code. Project Horizon infrastructure (2GW, 40,000+ GPUs) provides long-term compute cost advantages and independence from cloud provider pricing. CEO Jason Warner's GitHub CTO background provides credibility and enterprise relationships in the developer tools market. Bank and defense investor/customer overlap creates a flywheel of capital, validation, and data access.

regulatory.regulatory_exposure: GPAI provider. As a foundation model creator, Poolside falls under EU AI Act GPAI obligations for its European operations (Paris engineering team, Bpifrance investment). On-premises deployment model within customer security boundaries simplifies data residency compliance. Models fine-tuned on customer proprietary code raise questions about training data governance under EU AI Act transparency requirements. US-headquartered with significant French presence creates dual regulatory exposure (US executive orders on AI + EU AI Act). Defense contractor customers may trigger additional compliance requirements under national security frameworks.
